subject: Discovery: ShelfScale embeddings + rerank — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@shelfscale.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: ShelfScale embeddings + rerank — recap & next steps

Hi Taylor — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have a shared baseline and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections or gaps.

Key pain points you shared
- Search relevance has degraded as index size grew (we're at ~850M active chunks today, with projected growth to ~1.3B by Q4).
- Current reranking step is the biggest cost and latency contributor; you run a lightweight vector match first and then a transformer-based reranker that increases p50 -> p95 latency significantly.
- Nightly ingestion spikes (batches of ~120k vectors) cause background maintenance slowdowns and occasional query tail latency spikes.
- Observability is limited: SLOs for retrieval are not well-instrumented across the stack (embedding service, vector DB, reranker).

Current stack (from our discussion)
- Content store: S3 (chunk payloads), Postgres for metadata
- Vector store: Qdrant self-hosted fleet (k8s), use FAISS on disks for cold tier
- Embeddings: in-house encoder (open-encoder-v1) for production; small subset uses a managed embedding pipeline for experimental features
- Reranker: in-house transformer deployed on a small GPU fleet behind autoscaling policies

Success criteria you defined
- End-to-end (query -> top K reranked) p95 latency < 150ms, p99 < 300ms for critical routes
- Retrieval recall@10 >= 0.92 on the labeled eval set
- Cost target for production queries: ~<= $0.0010/query (blended embedding + retrieval + rerank cost)
- Pilot period: 6 weeks to validate latencies and cost with a 100M-vector pilot subset

Notes / constraints
- Data residency: US-only for now (may expand to EU next year)
- Security/compliance: SOC2 in scope — you asked about Redwood's evidence and onboarding timelines (see attachments)
- Ingestion pattern: bulk nightly batches (100k–150k) + continuous micro-batches during the day

Attachments I’m including
- SLS_infra_diagram.png — rough mapping I sketched during the call (vector tiers, rerank path, batching points)
- redwood-pricing-draft.pdf — preliminary pilot pricing and committed-capacity options
- sample_chunk_manifest.csv — template to share a small sample of your chunk metadata (if you can send a real sample it helps sizing)

Proposed next steps (please confirm availability)
1) You share a 1–2 day sample (or synthetic equivalent) of chunk manifests + a small embedding sample (we can sign an NDA if needed) — helps us estimate storage + index size.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team (30–45m) — proposed window: next Tue/Wed mornings PT. Karthik from our side will lead on routing, indexing, and batch policy options.
3) We'll produce a short pilot SOW (6 weeks) with target metrics and runbook for the 100M-vector pilot; Monica will own commercial terms.
4) We'll follow up with SOC2 evidence and a security questionnaire tailored to your needs.

If that all looks right I’ll start the SOW draft and calendar invites for the deep-dive. Thanks again — good first conversation.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

P.S. I noted your comment about reranker batching — Karthik, I flagged that for the deep-dive.
From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@shelfscale.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: ShelfScale embeddings + rerank — recap & next steps

Thanks Jordan — this looks correct and nicely organized. A few clarifications and answers below; I’ll loop in our infra lead if we move to a deep-dive.

Clarifications / additions
- Scale: our cold tier adds another ~200M vectors (archival, rarely queried) but active working set is ~850M now. Growth estimates to 1.3B are realistic.
- Vector DB: we run Qdrant 1.8 on a k8s autoscaling cluster today; we also keep nightly FAISS snapshots for recovery.
- Embeddings: we primarily use open-encoder-v1 (latency ~30ms per doc on CPU) — we do have a small subset of content using a managed transformer for higher-quality embeddings.
- Reranker: runs on a small GPU fleet (nvlink-enabled) — when load spikes we see p99 regressions driven by both queueing and KV-cache misses in the reranker.

Success criteria — confirming what we care about
- Retrieval recall@10 target: >= 0.92 on our priority dataset (matches what you wrote)
- End-to-end p95 target: < 150ms (we can tolerate occasional spikes during index maintenance)
- Cost: aiming for <= $0.00085/query blended — if you can show a path to ~0.0007 with a dedicated pilot that would be great for our finance team.

Files: I uploaded a small manifest and a 10k-row sample to the Drive link you proposed (folder: sample-manifests).

One question: for the pilot, how do you handle nightly bulk ingestion and the risk of tail latency during compaction/merge ops? Are there recommended batch windows or throttling knobs on the Redwood side?

We’re generally available for a technical deep-dive next Wed (Jul 22) 9–11am PT — let me know if that works for Karthik.

Thanks,
Taylor Nguyen
Head of IR & Search
ShelfScale
taylor@shelfscale.com
